label: <DEL> step of long (L=8-9) sequences starting with d or w
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, the step that outputs original token 0), and almost only in long sequences (L=9 holds 69% of mass, L=8 30%, L=7 1%, never L<=6). Output/first token is strongly concentrated: d (61% of mass, 34x lift), w (17%), then l, a, i, y. Never fires in original or copy phases. The predicate gets ~78% of mass but very low precision (~3%): most L>=8 sequences starting with d/w do not activate it, so it depends on more of the sequence content. Second token (next_out) g/i/h/l/r/2/u/y and the last original token b raise the rate, but no simple rule picks out the active cases (best F1 ~0.2). Magnitude grows with L (largest at L=9) and is highest for first_tok d; top examples are d...b sequences with L=8-9.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=d (+4.77), orig2=h (+3.14), phase=1 & out_tok=w (+3.14), orig2=g (+2.87), next_out=i (+2.24), prev_tok=b (+1.96). Lower it: in_first=0 (-4.32), orig7=- (-3.88), correct=1 (-3.26), orig6=- (-2.21).
